entries.sense_en: to free your mind of a secret or worry by telling it

synonyms.nuance: Admit a wrong or crime; unburden is broader and can be about any heavy worry.
Casual idiom for finally saying something that has been bothering you.
synonyms.example: I need to get this off my chest.

synonyms.nuance: Tell a secret to one trusted person, not to the whole world.
synonyms.example: She confided her fears to a friend.

entries.sense_en: in a short, clear way, using few words

synonyms.nuance: Simply short in time or length; succinctly also implies the wording is tight and clear.
Almost the same, but more common in writing and speeches about cutting extra words.
Short in a curt, slightly unfriendly way.

entries.sense_en: to explain something in detail

synonyms.nuance: The everyday word; expound is formal and suggests a long, learned explanation.
Add more detail to something already said.
Present facts or arguments clearly and in order.

entries.sense_en: a gentle, obedient nature that is easy to teach or manage

synonyms.nuance: Humble and quiet, often afraid to stand up for oneself.
Doing what you are told; docility is a natural gentle character, not just an act.
synonyms.example: the obedience of a trained dog

synonyms.nuance: Kind and soft in manner; says nothing about being controllable.

entries.sense_en: a person laughed at; the target of others' jokes

synonyms.nuance: A person everyone mocks; stronger and more humiliating.
synonyms.example: He became the laughingstock of the town.

synonyms.nuance: The regular target of people's teasing.
synonyms.example: He was the butt of their jokes.

synonyms.nuance: Common word for something funny; it doesn't usually mean the person being mocked.

entries.sense_en: to touch or stroke gently and lovingly

synonyms.nuance: Plain word for moving the hand gently over something; no special feeling required.
Quick, light taps rather than a long smooth movement.
Like caress but can sound uncomfortable or improper with people.

entries.sense_en: wise and quick to understand things; showing good judgment

synonyms.nuance: Having deep experience and good judgment; the everyday word.
Clever at practical matters, often about money or people.
Plain word for quick mind; sagacious is literary and stresses good judgment.

entries.sense_en: very small in value or worth; not worth respect

synonyms.nuance: Unimportant; says nothing about contempt.
Too small in amount, e.g. food or pay.
Small-minded, worrying about unimportant things.

entries.sense_en: very light, thin and easily broken, like spider web

synonyms.nuance: Thin and weak in a bad way; gossamer is delicate, sometimes pretty.
Fine and easily damaged, often with a positive feel.
Almost see-through, mostly about cloth.

entries.sense_en: not matching or fitting well with another's character

synonyms.nuance: Unable to live or work together; stronger and more technical.
Unpleasant or bad-tempered to be around.
Not showing understanding of another's feelings.

entries.sense_en: a special liking for something

synonyms.nuance: Warm, gentle liking; the everyday word.
Unfair preference that affects a decision.
Unfairly treating one person better; always negative.

entries.sense_en: slightly affected by a quality, having a trace of it

synonyms.nuance: Lightly colored or affected by a feeling; the most common match.
Has a hint of some quality; more casual.
Influenced by an attitude or feeling.

entries.sense_en: an indirect mention of something

synonyms.nuance: A general mention, direct or not.
synonyms.example: a reference to an old story

synonyms.nuance: A small clue about something hidden.
Different word: a false idea or appearance, often confused with allusion.

entries.sense_en: a person's natural way of thinking and reacting

synonyms.nuance: Nearly the same; stresses the usual mood.
Usually means a tendency to get angry.
The whole pattern of a person, not only emotional reactions.

entries.sense_en: lacking self-control, harsh and angry

synonyms.nuance: Going beyond reasonable limits, without the angry feel.
Simply too much.
Physical force or extreme intensity; stronger than intemperate language.

entries.sense_en: to treat someone or something cruelly

synonyms.nuance: Almost the same; a bit more common in speech.
Stronger, often repeated harm, physical or mental.
Failing to care for; not active cruelty.

entries.sense_en: to do something without hesitation or feeling any guilt about it

synonyms.nuance: Modern equivalent; feel no doubt about doing something questionable.
synonyms.example: He had no qualms about lying.

synonyms.nuance: Plain, neutral; no hint of moral doubt.
synonyms.example: She did not hesitate to speak.

synonyms.nuance: Casual; act without any second thought.

entries.sense_en: easily annoyed and complaining over small things

synonyms.nuance: Easily made angry; more general.
Casual; often for children or tired people.
Childishly sulky when one doesn't get one's way.

entries.sense_en: a place where someone often goes, here a bar

synonyms.nuance: Casual, friendly place where people meet.
Hidden, often shady place.
Familiar area where one often spends time; casual.

entries.sense_en: a strong wish to harm others

synonyms.nuance: Similar; the more common word, often about a specific act.
Petty wish to hurt or annoy someone, often out of resentment.
synonyms.example: She did it out of spite.

synonyms.nuance: Strong dislike; not necessarily wishing to harm.

entries.sense_en: deep, painful guilt about something wrong you did

synonyms.nuance: Sadness about something in the past; may not involve doing wrong.
Knowing you did wrong; remorse adds real sorrow.
Feeling bad about how others see you.

entries.sense_en: uncertain and mixed; not clearly one thing or the other

synonyms.nuance: Can be read in two ways; the common word.
Not clear or detailed at all.
Deliberately avoiding a direct answer.

entries.sense_en: to get rid of the effects of drink by sleeping

synonyms.nuance: Become sober, by any means.
synonyms.example: He needed time to sober up.

synonyms.nuance: Neutral; get better after something.
Get rid of a feeling or illness quickly.

entries.tip_ko: sleep it off: 자고 나서 (술이나 피로를) 털어내다.

entries.sense_en: was replaced by another feeling

synonyms.nuance: Modern usual form of the idiom.
Change into; less about one thing pushing out another.
Formal; stop resisting.

entries.sense_en: impossible to change or undo

synonyms.nuance: Cannot go back to the earlier state; used for changes and damage.
Last and not open to discussion.
Lasting forever; doesn't stress a decision.

entries.sense_en: the urge to do wrong or against reason, just because it is forbidden

synonyms.nuance: Habit of doing the opposite of what others want, often harmless.
Refusing to change; not necessarily against one's own interest.
More common form of the same word.

entries.sense_en: against, in spite of strong opposition

synonyms.nuance: Openly refusing to obey.
Plain, neutral; no sense of fighting against.
Simple opposition, less dramatic.

entries.sense_en: to trouble or distress, here to torment oneself

synonyms.nuance: Mild everyday irritation.
Stronger; causing long suffering.
Worry or disturb, more general.

entries.sense_en: to complete or finish, here the cruel act

synonyms.nuance: Everyday word; just finish.
Successfully achieve something aimed at.
Bring a hope or promise to reality.

entries.sense_en: a loop of rope that tightens, used for hanging

synonyms.nuance: A trap loop for catching animals.
Any circle of rope or string; not necessarily one that tightens.
A rope loop for catching cattle.

entries.sense_en: to put something in danger of loss or harm

synonyms.nuance: Put in physical or real danger.
Accept a chance of losing something.
Suggest harm may come; less about actual risk.

entries.sense_en: a very large, destructive fire

synonyms.nuance: Strong, bright fire; common in news.
A huge, terrifying fire, like hell.
General word, any size.

entries.sense_en: carved or cut into a surface

synonyms.nuance: Cut into wood or stone; everyday word.
Cut fine lines into metal, glass or stone.
Cut with acid or lines; also used for memories.

entries.sense_en: next to something

synonyms.nuance: Nearby and of the same kind, e.g. towns.
Everyday and simple.
Sharing a wall or border and joined.

entries.sense_en: the dead body of an animal

synonyms.nuance: A dead human body.
What is left of a body; gentle, formal.
General; dead or alive.

entries.sense_en: a ghostly image seen in the mind or imagination

synonyms.nuance: A ghost that suddenly appears.
Seeing something not there because of illness or drugs.
A false picture that seems real.

entries.sense_en: dull and confused, unable to think clearly, from drink

synonyms.nuance: Confused after a shock or blow.
Unable to feel or react.
Mixed-up mentally, often from alcohol or age.

entries.sense_en: a very large barrel for wine, beer or spirits

synonyms.nuance: General word for a wooden barrel.
Everyday word, any size.
A small barrel, mostly for beer.

entries.sense_en: to show a feeling or quality clearly

synonyms.nuance: Everyday word for making something visible.
Show openly, often deliberately.
Uncover what was hidden.

entries.sense_en: extreme hatred and disgust

synonyms.nuance: Sick feeling at something unpleasant; not always hate.
Strong hostility, often toward people.
Sudden physical-like disgust.

entries.tip_ko: loath(싫은)와 loathe(혐오하다)의 th 발음이 다릅니다: loathe는 /ð/.

entries.sense_en: stubborn, unwelcome persistence

synonyms.nuance: Neutral or positive; keeps going.
Firm holding on; usually admired.
Refusal to change; always negative.

entries.sense_en: not knowing what to do or say

synonyms.nuance: Confused by something hard to understand.
Unable to answer a question or solve a problem.
Unable to speak because of surprise.

entries.tip_ko: 'at a loss for words'로 자주 씁니다.

entries.sense_en: a wild fear or idea that is not real

synonyms.nuance: Pleasant imagined thing.
A false belief held strongly.
A hope that can never happen.

entries.sense_en: a wooden frame for hanging criminals

synonyms.nuance: Old word; a post where bodies were displayed after hanging.
Platform for executions, including beheading.
Only the rope loop, not the whole frame.

entries.sense_en: in human or physical form; the real embodiment of

synonyms.nuance: Given real form; used for ideas.
Shown as a person; stresses figure of speech.
Actually present, in person.
synonyms.example: I saw him in the flesh.

entries.sense_en: to make someone extremely angry and impatient

synonyms.nuance: Mild irritation.
Make very angry; more heated.
Bother repeatedly.

entries.sense_en: to push or provoke someone into a strong reaction

synonyms.nuance: Cause an angry reaction.
Encourage into action, often positive.
Casual; urge someone on to do something unwise.

entries.sense_en: a practical means or trick to solve a problem

synonyms.nuance: General answer to a problem.
A clever plan or trick.
Temporary fix.

entries.sense_en: to knock or pull something out of its fixed place

synonyms.nuance: General; take away.
Make less tight, not take out.
Casual; hit until it comes out.

entries.sense_en: the quality of being impossible to see into or understand

synonyms.nuance: Something not explained.
Hard to see or understand, not intentionally hidden.
Deliberate hiding.

entries.sense_en: in one direction and then back again

synonyms.nuance: Modern, more common in American English.
Vertical or along a length.
No sense of repeating direction.

entries.sense_en: by the way; changing the subject casually

synonyms.nuance: The modern everyday form.
synonyms.example: By the way, did you call her?

synonyms.nuance: More formal; adds a related side point.
Links to what was just said.

entries.sense_en: a false show of boldness

synonyms.nuance: Loud, empty talk.
Proud, showy way of walking or acting.
Real bravery; bravado is only pretense.

entries.sense_en: strange and different from what is normal

synonyms.nuance: Not normal; often medical or negative.
Everyday, mild.
Not following a pattern.

entries.sense_en: thick, dried blood from a wound

synonyms.nuance: Plain word for any blood.
Killing and violence, not blood itself.
Widespread killing and destruction.
